title: Security and Cryptography: Main Exam, 23 August 2018
instructions: ANSWER QUESTION ONE AND ANY OTHER TWO QUESTIONS

parts.text: Discuss biometrics as the strongest form of access control. Support your answer with an example of three types of biometrics.
Define the following terms in relation to computer systems security.
Confidentiality
Integrity
Non-repudiation
Briefly discuss SSL in relation to data security.
As a computer security expert for MKU, name two potential threats to the MIS. State three safeguard measures.
List five qualities of an efficient cryptosystem.
Define three security protocols that provide security to data in addition to facilitation of data and information exchange.
Expand the following acronyms.
Backdoor
Cracker
Salt
List four properties that can be used in an authentication system to vet the authorised system users.
As a security expert in Yahoo, discuss the need to implement digital signatures in email correspondence.
In relation to (a) above, suggest alternative mitigation measures to ensure security of emails.
You have been asked to do a risk assessment on all Airtel Money resources. Suggest the areas where the risk assessment would concentrate and why.
Discuss the best password management practices in securing a system.
Differentiate between the following authorisation systems.
Centralised and decentralised
Implicit and explicit

You have been hired as an IT human firewall trainer for Excel Ltd due to loopholes exploited by criminals to penetrate their systems. Briefly discuss the training areas for bank employees to curb social engineering.
Explain in detail how you would handle a cyber-attack incident in a hospital setup, bearing in mind that the information collected and stored in your organisation is highly confidential.
Discuss the various access control measures and suggest various suitable implementation areas for each.
State 5 limitations of implementing a firewall in a system.
Explain the importance of sound software testing in relation to the reduction of system vulnerability.
